title: cy-manifest v1 semantic predicates
//: NORMATIVE. Canonical wire validity is strict raw-JSON validation, plus the
pinned JSON Schema, plus the predicates in this file. JSON Schema cannot
express email-like author detection, canonical URL serialization, encoded
path inspection before URL parsing, or SemVer semantics; finite fixtures
cannot define an answer for every input. The algorithms and patterns here
are the definition. The corpora under corpus/ are conformance examples.
This artifact is pinned by $id and SHA-256 digest in ledger.json, and after
the first stable identity is issued a change here requires a new
formatVersion — otherwise it recreates the unselectable same-version
validator problem the schema identity split exists to solve.
The SDK reads this file rather than restating it, so the artifact is the
single source rather than a parallel copy that can drift.
A legal JavaScript identifier is not automatically a safe object key. The
host indexes installed apps and catalog entries in ordinary
prototype-bearing records, so `state.apps['toString'] !== undefined` is
true for an app that was never installed, and assigning to `__proto__`
mutates a record's prototype instead of creating an own property.
`cyweb` is the host's own federation name.

id.//: Never trimmed: surrounding whitespace makes it invalid, because trimming would silently accept a value that disagrees with the federation container name.

//: Two expectations per case, not one. `grammarPattern` is what the runtime
reader applies on every dev server and build; the rest is the submission
profile, applied only where a manifest is produced.
Build metadata is rejected because SemVer excludes it from precedence:
1.0.0+a and 1.0.0+b are distinct identities that tie for a latest
endpoint, and `+` in a URL path is an encoding hazard besides.
maxNumericIdentifier is not theoretical. Against node-semver@7.8.5,
The alternative is an arbitrary-precision comparator in the SDK, the Store
and the host.

limits.//: Code points, measured after the trim and normalization each field defines. The document limit is UTF-8 octets, which JSON Schema cannot express — the serializer enforces it.

//: Every property name and every string value must be a valid Unicode scalar
sequence, checked AFTER parsing. Strict UTF-8 validation of the raw bytes
does not catch this: the bytes of "\uDEAD" are plain ASCII. RFC 8259 §8.2
permits the escape and warns that consumer behaviour is unpredictable.
The name is extracted first, then re-checked. Taking `name` out of
{"name": "jane@example.org"} and publishing it would break the promise
that an author never carries an email address, so a name matching either
pattern omits the field with a readiness warning rather than publishing it.

repository.wireForm: https://host/path — no userinfo, no port, no query, no fragment, no trailing .git, no trailing slash
rejects: userinfo other than the conventional `git` of an SSH form
any percent escape in the path
//: An explicit port, query or fragment is REJECTED, not silently stripped:
dropping part of a URL changes what it addresses, and a developer who
wrote one deserves to be told. The `git@` of an SSH form is transport
syntax rather than a credential, which is the one userinfo exception.
Percent escapes are inspected on the RAW string, before any URL parser
normalizes them, and rejected outright — the same rule as
repositoryDirectory, for the same reason.

rejects: an absolute path or a leading /
repositoryDirectory.//: Banning the escape character outright is simpler than specifying recursive, case-insensitive percent-decoding that two implementations must match, and no legitimate monorepo path needs one.

homepage.wireForm: credential-free http(s) URL with path, query and fragment preserved
rejects: any scheme other than http or https
//: A port IS allowed, unlike repository: a local development URL is a
legitimate package value, which is also why plain http passes the producer
boundary. The Store's publication profile requires https for a public
listing; that is a Store rule, not a producer rule.
Trim, drop empties, de-duplicate, keep the first spelling and the authored
order, then apply the limits. Equality folds A-Z to a-z and compares every
other code point exactly — a portable rule two implementations can agree
on, unlike locale-aware case folding. When nothing survives, the field is
omitted rather than emitted empty.

emptyAfterTrim.source: A missing optional scalar, or a direct string empty after field-specific trimming, is absent and omitted. A supplied composite whose required member becomes empty — a repository object with a blank url — is invalid. A required name empty after trimming is invalid. Wrong types are always invalid.
emptyAfterTrim.wire: A present empty or untrimmed value is noncanonical and rejected. The Store never trims it and never omits it.

readinessWarnings.//: During the preview these are recommended, not required. The publication profile that decides which are mandatory is owned and versioned by the App Store; until it exists, a warning cannot cite a decision that has not been made.
